claims.paper_reference: PDF pp. 3-4 (Section IV-A), p. 6 (Section V-B), p. 12 (Appendix VIII-A, Eq. (24))
claims.statement: The PDF states k=3, n=m=768 and a 128.1-bit minimum. The current independent implementation instead selects k=6, n=m=1536; its complete archived seven-attack minimum is 136.475 bits.
claims.scope: Independent changed-parameter result only. Generic flattened-LWE/Gaussian-like estimator, declared ADPS16 quantum reduction model and GSA; coded-BKW retains its native word-operation convention. The preserved incomplete k=3 run contains a successful 51.94-bit attack estimate and cannot establish 128.1 bits. No actual-CDT, module-specific, implementation, all-attack or worst-case proof follows.
required_for_original_claim: Revise the PDF tuple and every dependent byte, airtime, resource and performance value together.
Supply original k=3 estimator inputs and complete attack logs if retaining that historical claim; do not overwrite the adverse independent record.
Justify security for the instantiated encryption distribution and declared threat model separately from heuristic attack-cost arithmetic.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 1 (abstract/contributions), p. 4 (Algorithm 1), p. 8 (Eq. (16)), p. 9 (Eqs. (17) and (19)), p. 11 (Eq. (23))
claims.statement: At the current k=6 tuple, packing at most 240 retained data coefficients plus 16 tags into one degree-256 polynomial reduces ciphertext payload from 14,336 to 7,168 bytes, compared with the two-polynomial raw path.
claims.scope: Structural encoded-payload arithmetic, not measured total wire savings. At 250 kbit/s the payload-only serialization bounds are 229.376 ms and 458.752 ms. Tickets, hashes/MACs, headers, fragmentation, retries and multihop transport are additional. Smaller L within one polynomial does not shorten an individual ciphertext.
required_for_original_claim: Replace the PDF's 8,192-to-4,096-byte and 131.072-ms numbers consistently if adopting k=6.
Publish full-protocol bytes and measured service costs before claiming end-to-end savings.
Evaluate the aggregate physical-signal distortion caused by retaining only part of the coefficient vector.

claims.statement: Host ciphertext addition and decryption implement addition of encoded quantized data/tag coefficients modulo p; data no-wrap checks permit a signed integer interpretation within the declared bound.
claims.scope: Preserved independent host functional executions are indexed by claim-coverage.json and the public archive. Exact encoded-coefficient aggregation does not imply exact aggregation of the physical samples through rounded integer lifting, selection and quantization. Randomized functional tests do not prove a 2^-128 decoding tail.
required_for_original_claim: State correctness in the encoded domain and retain plaintext no-wrap and decoding assumptions.
Provide aggregate-domain PRD/RMSE against the physical sum for every reported profile and admissible batch size.
Bind fresh execution receipts to the exact source, key/profile tuple, provider and input traces.

claims.statement: The host protocol binds signed tickets, profile/context/nonces and the exact authorized roster, and rejects tested compromised-gateway modifications and replay; the paper's integrity theorem remains conditional.
claims.scope: Independent real-provider functional trials, not a machine-checked QROM security reduction or attack-detection probability. Sources/sink and derivation secrets are trusted. Gateway-held HMACs do not secure a compromised gateway; the plaintext lightweight path is not confidential. Q_v/p^16 is one conditional tag-guessing contribution, not the complete security level.
required_for_original_claim: Make the one-distinct-report-per-ticket/source-offset rule an explicit theorem assumption and Algorithm 1 step.
Retain primitive-security, decoding, uniform-rejection and persistent-state assumptions in the reduction.
Document exact ML-DSA provider/version, nonce/profile/context binding, replay persistence and tested adversary capabilities.
Do not claim source-compromise, collusion, side-channel or availability resistance.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 4 (Algorithm 1), p. 6 (one-envelope statement), p. 7 (Seen and Eq. (13)); additional source-emission condition required by the implementation
claims.statement: SourceEmissionStore durably binds one payload and cached envelope to each ticket/source/nonce; ReplayStore enforces at-most-once sink acceptance. These are separate necessary conditions.
claims.scope: Inspectable SQLite host mechanisms and targeted regression tests. Two distinct reports under one hidden affine offset can permit 2*c1-c2 recombination. SQLite is not an embedded anti-rollback driver; Seen does not supply a durable result/outbox after a crash.
required_for_original_claim: Add durable bind/commit-before-release and same-envelope retries to Algorithm 1.
State anti-rollback/deletion and fresh-authorization requirements.
Supply board nonvolatile-storage and crash/recovery evidence if claiming deployed protection.
Keep at-most-once acceptance distinct from exactly-once result delivery.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 3 (Eq. (3)), p. 4 (capacities 16/14/12), p. 7 (epsilon_batch in Eq. (13)), p. 10 (profile correctness statements)
claims.statement: The independent k=6 actual finite-CDT calculation bounds decoding failure for profiles (sigma_enc,Nmax)=(3.2,16),(3.4,14),(3.6,12), including scaling carry; its 42-choice single-batch union log2 upper endpoint is approximately -130.5101732.
claims.scope: Executed outward-interval bound for the actual finite sampler, jointly over random key generation and one fresh honest batch. Profile/roster selection precedes fresh batch noises. It does not cover every fixed key, arbitrary observed-history conditioning, malicious ciphertexts, unlimited lifetime, memory or control dynamics. The second command requires Sage-enabled Python and creates a new run.
required_for_original_claim: Replace unsupported original k=3 correctness certificates with a matching revised tuple and probability statement.
Publish exact PMF/CDT, independence assumptions, carry/decoder analysis and interval endpoints.
Keep per-batch correctness separate from confidentiality, forgery, operational packet loss and finite-horizon risk.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 3 (Eq. (3)), p. 7 (Eq. (13)), pp. 7-8 (history-adaptive controller); the PDF gives no explicit finite-horizon risk budget
claims.statement: A declared multi-batch horizon requires an additional risk calculation; a single-batch 2^-128 target is not automatically a lifetime 2^-128 guarantee.
verification_commands: python tools/check_decoding_horizon.py --batches 6 --target-bits 128 # expected exit 2: risk budget exceeded
claims.scope: Executed exact-rational finite union budgets from the pinned single-batch bound: target 2^-128 permits at most 5 attempts (6 rejected); target 2^-120 permits at most 1458 (300 passes). No independence between failures is assumed. Each attempt must satisfy the stated fresh-noise and preselection conditions. This does not provide every-fixed-key/arbitrary-history conditional or lifetime guarantees and does not silently weaken a target.
required_for_original_claim: Specify task duration, maximum batch count, profile selection rule, roster rule and key-rotation schedule.
If claiming uniform fixed-key/history guarantees, provide a matching certificate/proof rather than reusing the joint random-key bound.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 3 (IntDb2/quantization pipeline), p. 5 (Algorithm 3), p. 13 (Eq. (25), Table III, PRD<=2.50% statement)
claims.statement: Table III's reported per-profile physical reconstruction quality does not establish fidelity of the current independent rounded-lifting aggregate against the true physical sum.
claims.scope: Actually executed and independently recomputed 72 declared synthetic cases (54 capacity-admissible, 18 inadmissible diagnostics), with exact integer arrays, rounding/selection/quantization attribution and explicit zero-reference PRD. Frozen source and raw inputs are public. This is aggregate-domain evidence for the current reference completion; it does not reproduce original Table III, its physical units or its threshold.
required_for_original_claim: Publish an identified signal corpus, physical units/scaling, sensor channel meaning, normalization, lifting/rounding, supports and boundary conventions.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 3 (Eqs. (1)-(4)), pp. 7-8 (Eq. (15), Algorithm 6, conditional boundedness theorem), p. 9 (calibration)
claims.statement: ControlledHMM, robust action scoring, DPP/HYS and evidence gates are implemented; the shipped synthetic model does not establish the PDF's calibrated closed-loop stability hypotheses.
verification_commands: python -m daahe replay-control --config configs/control_synthetic.json --telemetry examples/telemetry_synthetic.csv --method da-ahe --allow-synthetic --output runs/reviewer-synthetic-control.json
claims.scope: Functional/analytic implementation with explicitly uncertified fixtures. Artifact hash and tuple binding check identity, not proof validity. Conditional mean-square ultimate boundedness does not prove forward invariance, zero QoS violation or safety under arbitrary DoS. The second command is an uncertified inspection run.
required_for_original_claim: Publish separate training, heldout calibration and evaluation seeds/traces and the full observation/emission model.
Provide exact action library, P_V, Z_cert, gamma/beta, transition ambiguity/error radii and their uniform validity scope.
Provide a reviewed fallback supremum/nonemptiness certificate and an invariance argument or explicit exit handling.
Account for online kernel adaptation and bounded adversarial observations/disturbances in the theorem assumptions.
Supply a same-crypto DPP plus identical filter, no-belief robust filter and nominal-belief comparison before attributing performance to belief or robustness.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 3 (10-KiB gate in Eq. (3)), p. 4 (streaming memory discussion), p. 8 (setup), p. 13 (Table II)
claims.statement: The current independent core harness build is not evidence for the PDF's 10-KiB complete streaming workspace or 29,328-byte whole-firmware peak SRAM.
claims.scope: Physical samples=0. The indexed selected core build reports 5,624-byte load sections and 20,608-byte static RAM with reserved benchmark stack; this is not the complete Contiki-NG protocol, measured stack HWM or per-role 10-KiB certificate.
required_for_original_claim: Supply complete k=6 role-specific source, linked ELF/map, compiler/OS identities and buffer lifetimes.
Measure stack high-water and peak memory across encryption, transform, signatures/derivation/authentication, roster handling and network/interrupt paths.
Keep action workspace, total static SRAM, reserved stack and measured runtime peak distinct; avoid double counting.
Publish raw board capture with verified firmware identity before claiming physical resource results.

claims.paper_reference: PDF p. 8 (3.72M cycles, 58.125 ms, 1.395 mJ), p. 9 (Eqs. (17)-(21)), p. 10 (Table I), p. 13 (prototype description)
claims.statement: Historical nRF52840 timing/energy figures and the 77.199-ms weighted bound are unverified for the independent k=6 protocol.
claims.scope: Cross-compilation and host known answers are separate from physical timing/power. Simulator CPU service time and radio energy are declared modeling assumptions. Arithmetic payload airtime is not operational latency and cannot incorporate old k=3 CPU measurements to create a new k=6 total.
required_for_original_claim: Measure the complete k=6 source/gateway/sink paths with fresh raw cycles, clocks and power calibration.
Include ticket/signature/KDF/HMAC, source ledger, receive/listen, relay, OS/interrupt and fragmentation costs at the claimed boundary.
Bind trace intervals, voltage/current instruments and energy integration to firmware identity.
Recompute every workload-weighted expression from matching revised measurements.

claims.paper_reference: PDF pp. 9-10 (setup and Figs. 2-4), p. 11 (Fig. 5, Eqs. (22)-(23), ablations), p. 12 (Fig. 6 and conclusion)
claims.statement: The PDF's OMNeT++/INET 450.0-ms latency, 0.074%/0.098% residual loss, 33.0-s recovery and comparative improvements are not reproduced by the independent synthetic campaign.
claims.scope: Independent campaign: 3,000 sensors, 60 gateways, 90-s generation plus 35-s drain, 20 seeds/7 methods/140 runs, synthetic Python model. PDF: up to 5,000 nodes, 16 gateways, 300 s/30-s warm-up, OMNeT++6.0/INET4.4/RPL. All independent recovery records are right-censored; repair was not triggered. Model differences and adverse results must remain visible.
required_for_original_claim: Publish original simulator/routing/baseline code, exact configs, measured service calibration and all seed-specific traces/logs.
Run revised k=6 parameters with matched offered workload, integrity protection, fidelity constraints and action libraries across controllers.
Report effective verified delivery per exogenous opportunity, tail latency, censoring, loss/reject denominators and full-protocol energy/wire cost.
Use a disturbance that actually activates route repair before claiming its recovery contribution.
Retain paired-seed bootstrap inputs and report uncertainty without treating packets/nodes as independent replicates.

claims.paper_reference: Supports auditability of PDF p. 9 (paired seeds/statistics) and p. 12 (reproducibility statements); does not establish the historical numeric figures
claims.statement: A public immutable archive indexes 20 paired independent seeds, seven methods and 140 runs, with raw-to-summary recomputation and frozen-source replay interfaces.

New commands above are prospective, not new execution receipts. Exact historical replay uses frozen source and the documented macOS ARM64/Python3.12.10 environment; Linux raw recomputation is separate. Hashes establish bytes, not measurement truth.
required_for_original_claim: Describe this archive as independent synthetic evidence rather than recovered original-author experiments.
Archive any new execution with its own source/config/input/provider/environment identity.
Preserve historical evidence bytes, adverse outcomes, right-censoring and platform replay differences.
Add generated result hashes only after the new checks actually execute.
